items.title: Scoop: Lutnick stalled curbing Nvidia chip sales to China — again — after Oval Office showdown
items.excerpt: Per six sources, Trump has authorized a crackdown on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia AI chips to China three times this year, but Commerce Secretary Lutnick has repeatedly held back the export controls, including on Megaspeed. Commerce disputes the account.

history_match.title: The US let Nvidia sell chips to an empty office in China

items.title: Scoop: Inside Bessent's Situation Room confrontation with Lutnick over China chip security
items.excerpt: Sources say Treasury Secretary Bessent pressed Commerce on why Nvidia customer Megaspeed, accused of diverting U.S. AI chips to China, has not been added to the Entity List. Commerce spokesperson says the confrontation did not happen.

items.title: 젠슨황 스캔들로 美의회 '對中 칩규제 3법' 탄력…韓영향 주목
items.excerpt: 미 의회 양당 의원들이 AI 오버워치법·반도체 보안법(Chip Security Act)·매치법(MATCH Act) 등 대중 AI 반도체·장비 수출통제 3법을 국방수권법(NDAA)에 넣어 통과시키는 방안을 추진 중이다. 매치법은 동맹국의 장비 통제 강화를 압박해 삼성·SK 중국 공장에 영향이 예상된다.

items.title: 美 재무 "미중 정상, 내주 회동서 AI 대화 진전시킬 것"
items.excerpt: 베선트 미 재무장관은 18~19일 APEC 계기 선전 미중 정상회담에서 '초지능' 양자 대화가 진전될 것이라며, 첨단 모델 공개 전 평가·시험 모범사례를 논의하고 중대 사고 시 직접 연락 채널을 구축하기로 합의했다고 밝혔다.

items.title: 태국, 데이터센터 규제기준 마련…소음·온도·물 소비 등 제한
items.excerpt: AI 데이터센터 반대 여론 속에 태국 내각이 데이터센터 소음 70dBA 이하, 부지 경계 기온 상승 1~2도 이내, 냉각수 재순환 의무를 승인했다. 20MW 이상 시설은 산업단지에만 짓고 인허가는 원스톱으로 통합한다.

items.title: Governor Hochul launches NY AI research center; RAISE Act registration portal opens for large frontier AI developers
items.excerpt: New York opened a portal for large frontier AI companies to register and comply with RAISE Act safety, transparency and reporting requirements, and launched the New York Center for AI Responsibility and Research at SUNY Binghamton to independently test advanced AI systems. (Primary release; body date only — Nov 10, 2026.)

items.title: EU needs a system to respond to AI incidents, Finland and Estonia say
items.excerpt: In a letter seen by POLITICO, Finland and Estonia call for 'EU-level arrangements for responding to serious AI incidents' ahead of Friday's informal European Council in Dublin on AI.

items.title: EU needs only 'very trusted partners' on AI chips, tech chief says amid Nvidia crisis
items.excerpt: EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen says Europe wants only 'very trusted partners' for AI chips and sensitive industries as the Nvidia spy scandal unfolds.

items.title: EU watchdog probes Commission's AI pick over conflict of interest concerns
items.excerpt: The European Ombudsman will inspect Commission documents in an inquiry into the appointment of Siemens chair Jim Hagemann Snabe as EU AI envoy, over conflict-of-interest concerns.

items.title: AI has made it 'close to impossible' to assess university coursework, regulator says
items.excerpt: England's Office for Students says AI has made fair assessment of coursework nearly impossible and that institutions should return to traditional exams and in-person presentations, with sanctions possible for those that don't adapt.

items.title: Piggybacking to the Frontier: US data firms are selling RL environments to Chinese AI labs
items.excerpt: A ChinaTalk investigation finds at least nine US data vendors (incl. Mercor, Surge AI, AfterQuery, Turing) selling roughly $500M of training data and RL environments to Chinese AI labs, a channel outside chip export controls.

items.title: Political campaigns spent $187 million promoting AI-generated ads in the 2026 midterms. Did they work?
items.excerpt: Wesleyan Media Project data: about 300 AI-generated or AI-enhanced political ads ran in the 2026 midterms with roughly $187M in spending, ~90% from Republican candidates or allied groups; state deepfake-disclosure laws applied unevenly. (Body date Nov 11; time from RSS.)

items.title: Trump's 60 Minutes interview touched on AI safety, threat to arrest an AI exec
items.excerpt: In a 60 Minutes interview, Trump said 'I don't mind guardrails' for AI and discussed AI safety and a threat to arrest an AI executive.

items.title: Nancy Pelosi's replacement is ready to regulate AI
items.excerpt: Scott Wiener, author of California's SB 1047 and SB 53, made AI regulation a cornerstone of his career and is headed to Congress. (Low priority: profile, no new document.)
